top.title: Makinde Presents ₦1.115tn 2027 Budget To Oyo Assembly
top.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has presented a proposed budget of ₦1.115 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration and approval. Tagged the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, the proposal is valued at ₦1,115,341,378,359.90. Presenting the budget on Tuesday at the Assembly complex in Agodi, Ibadan, Makinde said it was designed to consolidate the gains of his administration and lay a foundation for sustainable development beyond its tenure. He described it as the final budget proposal of his administration, saying it would sustain the state’s development momentum and ensure continuity after the transition to a new government. “As we prepare to hand over the baton to the next administration, we bring before you the 2027 Budget of Sustained Progress. It is designed to consolidate our gains, sustain public services and carry our state’s development forward through the transition period and beyond,” he said. The governor said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, community development and the strengthening of public institutions, with significant allocations for capital projects in health, education and road infrastructure. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Makinde said Oyo State’s Internally Generated Revenue increased by 288 per cent, from ₦26.59 billion in 2019 to ₦103.25 billion in 2025. He also noted that the state ranked third nationally in the 2025 Subnational Ease of Doing Business Assessment. The governor said targeted interventions and partnerships had helped return about 65,000 out-of-school children to classrooms, alongside investments in educational infrastructure, recruitment and service delivery. He, however, said the administration’s performance should be measured beyond revenue figures and rankings. “Figures alone cannot fully assess our administration. The real measure of success is the impact we have made on the lives of our people and the institutions we have built to serve them beyond May 29, 2027,” he said. Makinde also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to women’s inclusion in governance, pledging to sustain the 35 per cent affirmative action policy for women. On infrastructure and agriculture, he said the government had prioritised strategic road projects to connect economic corridors, improve market access and create opportunities for farmers, businesses and rural communities. He said the establishment of the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency had helped reposition agriculture as a viable business sector, while the Oyo State Agribusiness Transformation Centre had become a hub for agricultural investment. top.title: Why Chiefs are reportedly trading two picks for Colts WR Josh Downs
top.description: Why Chiefs are reportedly trading two picks for Colts WR Josh Downs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs came into NFL trade deadline day with one very simple goal: acquire a wide receiver to help the offense. While Keenan Allen was dealt to the San Francisco 49ers , there was a different wide receiver from the Indianapolis Colts that they've had their eye on. Finally, with under half an hour to go, they made their move. According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer , the Chiefs are making a move for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs. In exchange for a pair of picks, the Chiefs are getting a new WR for Patrick Mahomes. Why Chiefs are trading for Josh Downs from Colts "Trade! The Chiefs are acquiring WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round and fifth-round picks, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports," Pelissero reports. Downs is a rental wide receiver for the Chiefs who instantly provides another solid weapon in the passing game for this offense. He'll join Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy in Kansas City, with running back Kenneth Walker III and tight end Travis Kelce making up a strong offensive supporting cast for Mahomes. The Chiefs are making this trade thanks in large part to Tyquan Thornton's season-ending injury. Add in that Worthy is banged up and has been underwhelming, and a WR addition was a must-have for this team. MORE : Harrison Butker keeps missing field goals and Chiefs fans have had enough A fourth-rounder and a fifth-rounder are a lot to give up for Downs for half a season and a seventh-round pick, but considering their major WR need and the other available options, this is a reasonable move for the Chiefs. Kansas City desperately needed WR help, and Downs might be the best WR traded in the middle of the 2026 season. Marvin Harrison Jr. went for a second-round pick and hasn't been great for the Houston Texans . The Chiefs, meanwhile, take a chance on Downs, who was having a down season with the Colts and their struggling offense. This move shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone, as the Chiefs were strongly implied as the favorites, and now, they're reportedly adding him in a huge move at the trade deadline. top.description: David Brytus-Imagn Images Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade reunion is a go as Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Minnesota Vikings were desperate to make a trade for a quarterback before the deadline after Monday night’s tough loss to the Buffalo Bills at home. Later in the day on Tuesday, they did just that , reuniting with a familiar face in the process. “Blockbuster! The Raiders are trading four-time Pro Bowl QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for their 2027 third-round pick,” reported NFL insider Tom Pelissero of The Ringer on X, formerly Twitter. The move reunites the Vikings with Cousins after he spent multiple seasons there with head coach Kevin O’Connell, finding considerable success in the process. Minnesota’s defense has been elite this year but its offense has stumbled, with neither Kyler Murray nor Carson Wentz finding consistent success under center, making it clear that the team had to make a change before the deadline. Mendoza has yet to make a start at the NFL level, but that will now change after he spent half of his rookie season learning behind Cousins. Cousins got off to a hot start to the year in Las Vegas, and although he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, he is still a competent veteran quarterback who should provide an upgrade for the Vikings immediately at the position. In any case, the Vikings will next hit the field on Sunday vs the Green Bay Packers, while Mendoza looks slated to make his first NFL start the same day vs the Seattle Seahawks. top.title: Broncos trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley
top.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers stands on the field during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick to the Chargers for Henley. Trade: Chargers are sending LB Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, per sources. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 10, 2026 Henley is a 6-0, 225-pound linebacker who was a third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2023 NFL Draft. Throughout his career, Henley has appeared in 56 games and totaled 317 tackles, 5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 4 interceptions, and 15 pass deflections during his time with the Chargers. This season, Henley has appeared in 8 games and totaled 51 tackles, 0.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 1 interception (which happened this past Sunday), and 2 pass deflections. Henley turns 27 years old here in a few days and is in the final year of his rookie deal, but figures to have a role in the Broncos’ defense moving forward. In the short term, Henley will play behind veteran starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , according to reports, but he is a talented linebacker who can cover and blitz, so he should earn some playing time rather quickly. The Broncos are sending a 2027 4th-round pick to the Chargers, but are expected to get a 4th-round compensation pick due to John Franklin-Myers signing with the Titans in free agency this offseason. I really like this pick. Henley is a talented player who gives the Broncos something they really need. An athletic linebacker with sideline-to-sideline speed that can cover and cover well. He’s an excellent coverage linebacker and can cover tight ends and running backs in the pass game, which has been a multi-year issue for the Broncos. Justin Strnad has graded out as one of the better coverage linebackers in the NFL, while Alex Singleton has struggled in that area. Singleton has been solid in the run game, but if he were to come off the field on third downs for Henley, I think that would improve the Broncos’ third-down defense. However, we have to see how the Broncos handle this moving forward, but obviously they have a vision for him since they traded for him. With Henley in the final year of his deal, and the fact that the Broncos traded a 4th-round pick for him, he seems like a player the team views as part of their future. Time will tell there, but it seems like a move for a player they plan on having beyond this season.

top.title: Shawn Horcoff Addresses the Dylan Larkin Trade Standoff
top.description: Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff met with reporters at the NHL general managers’ meetings in Toronto on Tuesday, and nothing he said moved either of the two situations hanging over his roster. Asked about the Dylan Larkin trade standoff and Simon Edvinsson’s unsigned contract, Horcoff said it was “status quo” with both players. Oct 26, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; Edmonton Oilers defensemen Ryan Shea (6) looks to clear the puck in front of Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) during the second period at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Horcoff declined to comment on Dylan Larkin’s trade list The one detail that would tell everyone how close this is to ending stayed off the table. Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com reported that “Horcoff declined to comment on whether Larkin has altered the list of teams to which he would agree to be traded.” Horcoff did describe what a resolution has to look like from Detroit’s side. “Ideally, we get something that works for both sides, right?” he said . “But it has to be something that helps this team.” Larkin still has only 10 teams on his list The Red Wings would like Larkin to open up his approved list, and so far it has not changed. TSN’s Pierre LeBrun reported that Detroit has exhausted its options with the current 10 teams and would like to go deeper in talks with six to eight clubs outside them, while Larkin’s camp believes the list is already long enough. As long as it stays at 10, the market Detroit can actually work is small. Per LeBrun, the 10 teams are the New Jersey Devils, the Colorado Avalanche, the Vegas Golden Knights, the Dallas Stars, the Minnesota Wild, the Washington Capitals, the Utah Mammoth, the Carolina Hurricanes, the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Florida Panthers. Larkin is suspended without pay for now, which means Horcoff and the Red Wings can take their time with a trade. The 30-year-old center has played in 10 games this season for the Red Wings. Larkin scored two goals and recorded four assists with a plus-3 rating, according to ESPN . Horcoff still wants to sign Simon Edvinsson The other half of the status quo carries a hard date. Edvinsson, 23, is an unsigned restricted free agent working out in Nashville, and Cotsonika reported that the defenseman must sign by Dec. 1 to be eligible to play this season. Horcoff has said he has no interest in trading Edvinsson, and on Tuesday he did not close the door on listening. “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls,” Horcoff said. He added that his job is to do what is in the best interest of the Red Wings, and that he will take those calls and hear what other teams have to say.

top.title: Kyle Busch’s Hauler Drives Away For The Final Time At Homestead
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The No. 8 hauler left Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday night for the very last time, marking a somber end to the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season. After the championship race concluded, the 1.5-mile track was exited by this massive truck, which bore the signature of the late Kyle Busch, as it drove through the tunnel. Fans watched a video by Motorsport showing the team loading up the equipment out of deep respect for the driver who won 234 races across the top three series before his sudden death in May. Austin Hill took over the ride for Richard Childress Racing, piloting the No. 33 Chevrolet to a 15th-place finish in the finale. The team changed the car number from 8 to 33 to honor Busch, yet they kept the old hauler on site until this final departure. In 2027, Hill is scheduled to return full-time to the No. 33, shouldering a season marked by both a championship and a tragedy. His best effort this year came at Talladega with a 14th-place result, but Sunday was about saying goodbye. A Season of Highs and Lows The 2026 season will forever be remembered for two Kyles: Kyle Larson’s dominant playoff surge and Kyle Busch’s shocking death. Larson clinched his third Cup Series title during the opening stage of the finale, finishing 12th at Homestead-Miami Speedway to cap a 49-point victory over Christopher Bell. Even though Larson became the 11th driver in history to win three titles, he refused to look back at his achievements while the sport mourned. “I just feel like when you’re in it and you’re competing, it’s just so hard to reflect in the moment,” Larson said, according to a report . He added that he still has more to accomplish and plans to keep looking out the windshield rather than stopping to admire the rearview mirror. The championship celebration at the annual awards banquet on Tuesday will likely name Busch the most popular driver, honoring a man who died after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis. Final Tributes At The Track NASCAR leadership made sure the memory of “Rowdy” stayed front and center during the final race. Every fan in the grandstands received a No. 8 Busch flag, and a memorial graphic dedicated to him was painted directly on the frontstretch. The NBC TV booth observed a silent Lap 8 in his honor, with many attendees holding up eight fingers to pay tribute to the two-time champion. “It’s tough to not talk about Kyle when you’re back in Miami,” NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell said. He described Busch as an extraordinary competitor who won the championship at this very track and left a forever mark on the sport. O’Donnell admitted that celebrating a championship feels different without him, noting that the community still misses him deeply. Busch won both of his Cup titles in 2015 and 2019 at Homestead, making his final farewell at this venue even more poignant.

top.title: 😳 384 logos on one shirt? Club plans craziest stunt ever
top.description: 😳 384 logos on one shirt? Club plans craziest stunt ever Why have one big main sponsor when you can have 384 (!)? Yes, you read that right: Brazilian club São Joseense, from the state of Paraná, is flipping the script for the 2027 season. Instead of signing a single mega-deal, the club is turning its new shirt into a colorful mosaic for the local community, with a whopping 384 advertising spaces. Each advertising space measures a compact 3.5 by 3.5 centimeters. Depending on whether the logo takes pride of place on the chest or ends up nearer the hem, interested sponsors will pay between 2,000 and 15,000 reais (roughly €300 to €2,500). But what is the club hoping to achieve? According to a press release, the aim is to give small businesses the chance to buy advertising space on the club's shirt. "Being a main sponsor costs a lot of money, which severely limits who can get involved. Our shirt project now gives microbusiness owners and sports enthusiasts an affordable way in," explained Eduardo Grassi. The club's managing director also emphasized: "We want business owners and fans to feel part of this sporting journey—in a city that lives and breathes football but has until now lacked a team of its own to identify with. This is another step toward making São Joseense more prominent and better equipped for a year full of sporting challenges awaiting us in 2027." Among other things, the club will make its debut in the prestigious Brazilian cup competition, the Copa do Brasil. For the mini-sponsors, that means exposure and TV airtime that microbusinesses can usually only dream of. Once the design is finalized, the shirts may well look like a giant QR code from a distance. But in the stands and among local businesses, the initiative is probably already creating exactly what every club hopes for: the feeling of being out on the pitch together. 📸 Instagram São Joseense This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. The independent panel determined City had intended to breach financial rules by inflating revenues or reducing costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion at the current exchange rate), through a series of 'sham' arrangements. top.description: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. top.title: Santi Aldama Fixes Dallas Offense After Brutal Losses
top.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Mavericks finally found their rhythm on Sunday night, crushing the Brooklyn Nets by a staggering 37-point margin. This 130-93 victory marks the team’s largest winning streak of the season so far. Following a slump marked by consecutive defeats against the Sacramento Kings and San Antonio Spurs, the victory arrives. Per The Smoking Cuban , this sharp turnaround coincides directly with the return of Santi Aldama to the starting lineup. Aldama is filling a roster spot and solving specific problems that plagued the offense all year. The team struggled mightily in their last game against Utah, shooting just 41.9 percent from the field and a poor 28.1 percent from three-point range. However, the energy shifted instantly when Aldama got back on the court. According to The Smoking Cuban , the Mavericks have improved considerably in offensive rebounding and second-chance points specifically because of his presence. The Second-Chance Fix For a long time, Dallas could not secure loose balls near the rim. Throughout the whole league last year, the squad placed 22nd for offensive rebounding and 24th for second-chance points. One year prior, the Mavericks ranked among the NBA’s poorest scoring teams after a missed shot. That stat line has flipped in a hurry. Against the Utah Jazz, Dallas outrebounded the opponent 21-8 on the offensive glass. This dominance led to a massive 21-5 advantage in second-chance points. Aldama alone grabbed nine rebounds in that game, with four of them coming on the offensive end. Versatility Creates Mismatches The big man’s size alone gives Dallas a bonus that other teams cannot match. He is not pigeonholed into playing only center or power forward, which changes how the offense flows. His shooting skill enables Aldama to occupy the three position, He played even when paired with Morez Johnson Jr. in lineups and Daniel Gafford. His perimeter game was on full display against Brooklyn, where he scored 12 points. He shot 5-of-7 from the floor and hit 2-of-4 from three-point range. Aldama scored in a variety of ways, including a basket off a dribble drive that showed his unique skill set. A New Offensive Identity The length and versatility Aldama brings have already stood out in these recent wins. The 7-foot big man helps the team handle defensive pressure and creates easy looks for teammates. His ability to stretch the floor opens up driving lanes for guards who were previously clogged. The improvement in both rebounding and scoring options suggests the team is only getting better. Per The Smoking Cuban, Aldama is a key reason the Mavericks are now two games above .500.

top.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
top.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. nigeria.title: Awujale stool: Adele-in-Council sues Abiodun, challenges reconstituted interregnum committee
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council has dragged the Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, and members of the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council before the state High Court, Ijebu-Ode, challenging what it described as an unlawful attempt to displace the traditional administrative structure of Ijebuland. Other defendants sued alongside Gov Abiodun are the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs as well as members of the recently reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council including High Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu Ode, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa, Prof Jide Ajayi, the Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen Bakare, the Babalaje as well as Chief Alade Shote, the Otun Balogun The suit dated November 5, 2026 and marked HCJ/201/2026 according to a statement from the Media office of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council and supporting court documents made available to journalists on Tuesday seeks to establish the authority of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council to oversee the traditional and administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum following the transition of the late Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Kayode Adetona. The nine members of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council led by the Adele and Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland, Olorogun Dr Sonny Kuku, are asking the court to declare that the Adele system is the only legitimate traditional administrative authority recognised by the native law, customs and ancestral practices of the Ijebu people during the period between the reigns of successive Awujales. They are also challenging the establishment and subsequent reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, describing the arrangement as alien to Ijebu customary law and inconsistent with the Ogun State Chiefs Law. In the substantive suit, the plaintiffs are seeking a declaration that neither the state governor nor the relevant government authorities possess the power to create or reconstitute an administrative council capable of displacing the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during an interregnum. nigeria.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation Of Up To $1.4 Trillion
nigeria.description: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, putting the company’s total valuation at up to $1.4 trillion. The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of “between $70.00 and $78.00” per share, amounting to $64.3 billion. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16. This photograph shows the logo of the US artificial intelligence safety and research company Anthropic displayed on a smartphone’s screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP On Monday, the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions. Through these characters, Azubike considers a familiar experience for women: the pull between what an occasion expects and what an individual wants to express. Every woman who has dressed for an occasion has encountered this tension in some form, whether in choosing to honour a tradition or finding room to express herself within it. The garments give form to this conversation. The Cloister Dress is paired with the Banner Dress, while the Manor Jumpsuit is placed alongside the Assembly Set. entertainment.description: Africa’s tech icon and Chairman of Zinox Group , Leo Stan Ekeh , has told an international gathering of women leaders that his decision to build a technology company in Africa, at a time when the sector was virtually non-existent on the continent, amounted to what he described as “corporate suicide”. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. He said he returned from his studies abroad to a Nigeria where his peers were filing into banking, oil and gas, and where technology was largely seen as a foreign game. Ekeh, who studied Economics in India, said he was discouraged from pursuing a postgraduate degree in Computer Science in Europe because of the prevailing perception then that Africa might have little need for computers over the next 35 years, potentially leaving him frustrated. He subsequently opted for a postgraduate degree in Risk Management before pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Law (LLM) at London Guildhall University. He recalled that he could not sit his final law examinations because he had diverted his tuition fees into his passion for technology entrepreneurship. He also disclosed that he had fended off recruitment attempts by international technology companies that had sought to hire him before his return to Africa. “I chose the road not taken,” he told the conference. “It was corporate suicide in the eyes of my parents and many others. I lost the fear because I believed technology was the master key that would unlock possibilities for Nigeria and Africa.” He said the journey came with considerable hardship, including living on one meal a day for over three years and sleeping in a very small room in his office. According to him, his vision was to create a Nigerian and, by extension, an African IT identity. Recalling the launch of his first company, Task Systems Ltd, over 35 years ago, the company that pioneered desktop publishing and computer graphics in Nigeria. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick to the Chargers for Henley. Trade: Chargers are sending LB Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, per sources. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 10, 2026 Henley is a 6-0, 225-pound linebacker who was a third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2023 NFL Draft. Throughout his career, Henley has appeared in 56 games and totaled 317 tackles, 5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 4 interceptions, and 15 pass deflections during his time with the Chargers. This season, Henley has appeared in 8 games and totaled 51 tackles, 0.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 1 interception (which happened this past Sunday), and 2 pass deflections. Henley turns 27 years old here in a few days and is in the final year of his rookie deal, but figures to have a role in the Broncos’ defense moving forward. In the short term, Henley will play behind veteran starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , according to reports, but he is a talented linebacker who can cover and blitz, so he should earn some playing time rather quickly. The Broncos are sending a 2027 4th-round pick to the Chargers, but are expected to get a 4th-round compensation pick due to John Franklin-Myers signing with the Titans in free agency this offseason. I really like this pick. Henley is a talented player who gives the Broncos something they really need. An athletic linebacker with sideline-to-sideline speed that can cover and cover well. He’s an excellent coverage linebacker and can cover tight ends and running backs in the pass game, which has been a multi-year issue for the Broncos. Justin Strnad has graded out as one of the better coverage linebackers in the NFL, while Alex Singleton has struggled in that area. Singleton has been solid in the run game, but if he were to come off the field on third downs for Henley, I think that would improve the Broncos’ third-down defense. However, we have to see how the Broncos handle this moving forward, but obviously they have a vision for him since they traded for him. With Henley in the final year of his deal, and the fact that the Broncos traded a 4th-round pick for him, he seems like a player the team views as part of their future. Time will tell there, but it seems like a move for a player they plan on having beyond this season.

sports.title: Shawn Horcoff Addresses the Dylan Larkin Trade Standoff
sports.description: Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff met with reporters at the NHL general managers’ meetings in Toronto on Tuesday, and nothing he said moved either of the two situations hanging over his roster. Asked about the Dylan Larkin trade standoff and Simon Edvinsson’s unsigned contract, Horcoff said it was “status quo” with both players. Oct 26, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; Edmonton Oilers defensemen Ryan Shea (6) looks to clear the puck in front of Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) during the second period at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Horcoff declined to comment on Dylan Larkin’s trade list The one detail that would tell everyone how close this is to ending stayed off the table. Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com reported that “Horcoff declined to comment on whether Larkin has altered the list of teams to which he would agree to be traded.” Horcoff did describe what a resolution has to look like from Detroit’s side. “Ideally, we get something that works for both sides, right?” he said . “But it has to be something that helps this team.” Larkin still has only 10 teams on his list The Red Wings would like Larkin to open up his approved list, and so far it has not changed. TSN’s Pierre LeBrun reported that Detroit has exhausted its options with the current 10 teams and would like to go deeper in talks with six to eight clubs outside them, while Larkin’s camp believes the list is already long enough. As long as it stays at 10, the market Detroit can actually work is small. Per LeBrun, the 10 teams are the New Jersey Devils, the Colorado Avalanche, the Vegas Golden Knights, the Dallas Stars, the Minnesota Wild, the Washington Capitals, the Utah Mammoth, the Carolina Hurricanes, the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Florida Panthers. Larkin is suspended without pay for now, which means Horcoff and the Red Wings can take their time with a trade. The 30-year-old center has played in 10 games this season for the Red Wings. Larkin scored two goals and recorded four assists with a plus-3 rating, according to ESPN . Horcoff still wants to sign Simon Edvinsson The other half of the status quo carries a hard date. Edvinsson, 23, is an unsigned restricted free agent working out in Nashville, and Cotsonika reported that the defenseman must sign by Dec. 1 to be eligible to play this season. Horcoff has said he has no interest in trading Edvinsson, and on Tuesday he did not close the door on listening. “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls,” Horcoff said. He added that his job is to do what is in the best interest of the Red Wings, and that he will take those calls and hear what other teams have to say.

sports.title: Kyle Busch’s Hauler Drives Away For The Final Time At Homestead
sports.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The No. 8 hauler left Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday night for the very last time, marking a somber end to the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season. After the championship race concluded, the 1.5-mile track was exited by this massive truck, which bore the signature of the late Kyle Busch, as it drove through the tunnel. Fans watched a video by Motorsport showing the team loading up the equipment out of deep respect for the driver who won 234 races across the top three series before his sudden death in May. Austin Hill took over the ride for Richard Childress Racing, piloting the No. 33 Chevrolet to a 15th-place finish in the finale. The team changed the car number from 8 to 33 to honor Busch, yet they kept the old hauler on site until this final departure. In 2027, Hill is scheduled to return full-time to the No. 33, shouldering a season marked by both a championship and a tragedy. His best effort this year came at Talladega with a 14th-place result, but Sunday was about saying goodbye. A Season of Highs and Lows The 2026 season will forever be remembered for two Kyles: Kyle Larson’s dominant playoff surge and Kyle Busch’s shocking death. Larson clinched his third Cup Series title during the opening stage of the finale, finishing 12th at Homestead-Miami Speedway to cap a 49-point victory over Christopher Bell. Even though Larson became the 11th driver in history to win three titles, he refused to look back at his achievements while the sport mourned. “I just feel like when you’re in it and you’re competing, it’s just so hard to reflect in the moment,” Larson said, according to a report . He added that he still has more to accomplish and plans to keep looking out the windshield rather than stopping to admire the rearview mirror. The championship celebration at the annual awards banquet on Tuesday will likely name Busch the most popular driver, honoring a man who died after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis. Final Tributes At The Track NASCAR leadership made sure the memory of “Rowdy” stayed front and center during the final race. Every fan in the grandstands received a No. 8 Busch flag, and a memorial graphic dedicated to him was painted directly on the frontstretch. The NBC TV booth observed a silent Lap 8 in his honor, with many attendees holding up eight fingers to pay tribute to the two-time champion. “It’s tough to not talk about Kyle when you’re back in Miami,” NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell said. He described Busch as an extraordinary competitor who won the championship at this very track and left a forever mark on the sport. O’Donnell admitted that celebrating a championship feels different without him, noting that the community still misses him deeply. Busch won both of his Cup titles in 2015 and 2019 at Homestead, making his final farewell at this venue even more poignant.

Yes, you read that right: Brazilian club São Joseense, from the state of Paraná, is flipping the script for the 2027 season. Instead of signing a single mega-deal, the club is turning its new shirt into a colorful mosaic for the local community, with a whopping 384 advertising spaces. Each advertising space measures a compact 3.5 by 3.5 centimeters. Depending on whether the logo takes pride of place on the chest or ends up nearer the hem, interested sponsors will pay between 2,000 and 15,000 reais (roughly €300 to €2,500). But what is the club hoping to achieve? According to a press release, the aim is to give small businesses the chance to buy advertising space on the club's shirt. "Being a main sponsor costs a lot of money, which severely limits who can get involved. Our shirt project now gives microbusiness owners and sports enthusiasts an affordable way in," explained Eduardo Grassi. The club's managing director also emphasized: "We want business owners and fans to feel part of this sporting journey—in a city that lives and breathes football but has until now lacked a team of its own to identify with. This is another step toward making São Joseense more prominent and better equipped for a year full of sporting challenges awaiting us in 2027." Among other things, the club will make its debut in the prestigious Brazilian cup competition, the Copa do Brasil. For the mini-sponsors, that means exposure and TV airtime that microbusinesses can usually only dream of. Once the design is finalized, the shirts may well look like a giant QR code from a distance. sports.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Mavericks finally found their rhythm on Sunday night, crushing the Brooklyn Nets by a staggering 37-point margin. This 130-93 victory marks the team’s largest winning streak of the season so far. Following a slump marked by consecutive defeats against the Sacramento Kings and San Antonio Spurs, the victory arrives. One year prior, the Mavericks ranked among the NBA’s poorest scoring teams after a missed shot. That stat line has flipped in a hurry. Against the Utah Jazz, Dallas outrebounded the opponent 21-8 on the offensive glass. This dominance led to a massive 21-5 advantage in second-chance points. A New Offensive Identity The length and versatility Aldama brings have already stood out in these recent wins. sports.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
sports.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. technology.title: To thwart reverse engineering by agents, dev proposes blinding them
technology.description: Now that LLMs can help analyze commercial software binaries and recreate their functionality, one software developer and student has created a project designed to make this process more difficult. Timo Zhang's project is called Blind LLM Agents (BLA), and as its name suggests, it attempts to interfere with efforts by AI agents to scrutinize app code. "Coding agents can reverse-engineer shipped packages, CLIs, and WASM in minutes," Zhang told The Register in an email. "Classic obfuscation was built for humans and static tools, not LLMs that reason about meaning. Blind LLM Agents is a protection layer for that threat model." Such agents can also help developers build alternatives to existing commercial software. Last month, Artcraft , a two-person development shop, released seven open-source apps that aim to be replacements for Adobe's commercial apps Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. Artcraft claims these apps are "clean-room reimplementations" written from scratch in Rust using Anthropic Opus 5.5. Setting aside the question of whether enlisting an AI model to reimplement an app really immunizes the creator from legal risk, those making apps face the possibility that someone will have an LLM probe published app binaries and reconstruct them through reverse engineering. There's in fact a framework for this, Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). Zhang has faced some criticism on social media for creating a limited barrier to copying other people's work (which at this point might simply be the work of another LLM). But not everyone accepts that all publicly accessible binaries should be easily available for review and reuse. BLA cannot prevent committed reverse engineering efforts, but it may add a bit of friction to the process when LLMs are involved. "It doesn't write app code — it hardens what you've already built," Zhang said. "A transform pipeline (plus MCP tools / an agent Skill) applies renaming, lane splitting, seed-derived string encryption, build polymorphism, WASM export renaming, decoys, self-seal integrity checks, and a coverage matrix that won't claim protection it can't prove. Behavior stays equivalent; recovery cost goes up." Zhang said various evaluations like red teaming and CrackMe challenges to recover keys or flags from hardened artifacts show that BLA is effective. "We also drive REA (a reverse-engineering agent) against those builds," he said. "Fail-to-break is the pass. CI tracks defense score, self-verifies integrity coverage, and checks functional equivalence. We raise the cost — we don't claim it is unbreakable." The project website says as much, noting that it raises the effort for analysis and adds decoy code, but doesn't promise protection against traditional interactive reverse engineering tools like Ghidra or Frida. technology.description: Security company Barracuda warns that attackers are exploiting a pre-authentication authorization bypass bug and a command-injection vulnerability in its popular Email Security Gateway (ESG) products that, when chained, could allow the crims to run commands with root privileges. “We have identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations,” the security vendor said in a late Monday night update to its earlier security advisory. Barracuda declined to answer The Register ’s questions, including one about how many organizations have been hit by attackers. A company spokesperson told us that it “worked directly” with the affected businesses “to quickly address the issue. Barracuda acted promptly to remediate the vulnerabilities, releasing patches for affected products.” The vendor disclosed and fixed the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 , last week. CVE-2026-116606 is a 9.3 CVSS-rated, pre-authentication authorization bypass flaw in ESG. At the time, the vendor did not report any active exploitation of either. We don’t yet know who is responsible for the attacks, or whether the intruders gained root access – but if they did, they could steal data, install backdoors, and take full control of affected systems. These types of edge-device exploits have been used by Chinese-government spies , and in 2023 the FBI blamed PRC-linked attackers for a series of attacks that targeted Barracuda ESGs to deploy custom malware and maintain access to high-value networks . science.description: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. If we compare these planets to Earth , which has a stable magnetic field tilted by just 11 degrees to our planet’s rotation, we can see how extreme the magnetic fields of the ice giants are. Various explanations for the strange magnetic fields of the ice giants have been put forward over the years. Uranus as a whole is tilted by 97 degrees and effectively rolls around the sun , and speculation is that billions of years ago it was knocked on its side by a collision with a long-lost Earth-sized planet. Could this collision have also skewed its magnetic field? This might be a plausible explanation were Neptune’s magnetic field also not similarly skewed without having experienced a collision. Clearly, whatever the cause, it must be intrinsic to the nature of the two ice giant planets. Now, a new study by scientists in the U.S. and the UK, based on computer simulations and Voyager 2’s measurements of the two planets’ magnetic fields, may have found a solution. The solution to the weird magnetic fields of the solar system's ice giants may come down to how planets generate their magnetic field through the dynamo effect. This arises from the swirling, convective motion of an electrically conducting liquid within a rotating body, which is able to generate and maintain a powerful magnetic field. Inside Earth, the electrically conducting fluid is the molten iron in the outer part of our planet’s core, and the magnetic field that it generates has clear north and south poles – what we call a dipole, a phenomenon that we can also see in the two magnetic poles of a simple bar magnet. However, the conditions inside Uranus and Neptune are somewhat different. As ice giants, they contain a lot of volatiles – ammonia, hydrogen, helium, methane, and water surrounding a probable rocky core. Furthermore, Uranus and Neptune are substantially larger than Earth , with 14.5 and 17 times the mass of our planet, respectively. This increased mass creates crushing conditions within the interior of the ice giants. Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

In the final weeks of 1960, two young radio enthusiasts were monitoring transmissions from a home-built listening station on a rooftop in Turin, Italy, when the brothers detected something extraordinary: a faint signal that bore the hallmarks of one originating from space. That wasn't the only surprising thing about the alleged signal:, the transmission carried a very familiar message: it was Morse code for the international distress signal SOS. As the youths listened, the signal seemed to grow weaker. This raised a troubling possibility: could it be that the signal's source was moving farther away from Earth ? And if so, was it possible that this concerning signal was of Soviet origin — perhaps a spacecraft drifting helplessly into space, carrying a cosmonaut on board whose doomed mission had never been publicly acknowledged? These strange events from November 1960 became the first in a series of alleged radio signal interceptions that would form the basis of an enduring Cold War-era mystery involving so-called "lost cosmonauts" — early Soviet space travelers rumored to have died during secret spaceflight missions before Yuri Gagarin's historic flight the following spring, in April 1961.Today, more than six decades later, the story remains one of the most haunting legends of the Space Age. Were there truly early Soviet space missions — with tragically ill-fated cosmonaut crews — that remain undisclosed to this day? science.description: 5 min read NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy. Watch to learn how the presence of a planet modifies the gravitational wave signal from tightly orbiting white dwarfs. The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory could detect a Jupiter-mass planet in such systems up to thousands of light-years away. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Download high-resolution video from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio “The most common source for LISA is expected to be double white dwarf systems, which are binaries composed of white dwarfs in tight orbits,” said Casey McGrath, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. “If an exoplanet also orbits within one of these systems, its presence becomes imprinted on the gravitational wave signal in a way we’ll be able to uncover.” Two papers published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal detail the findings. The first , authored solely by McGrath, examines the detection method and determines the planet masses and orbital periods where it would work best. The second paper , by McGrath and coauthors, investigates how such planets could be confirmed using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope . The possibility of detecting exoplanets around LISA double white dwarf systems was first proposed by Japanese astronomer Naoki Seto in 2008. Led by ESA (European Space Agency), the LISA mission is slated for launch in the mid-2030s. As a collaborative partner, NASA is contributing the telescopes, other critical hardware, and engineering and scientific support as part of its mission to better understand how the universe works. The LISA detection method is similar to one called radial velocity that uses light and is already employed to find exoplanets around nearby stars. As a planet orbits, its gravity tugs on its host star, imparting a small reflex motion, or wobble, onto it. This wobble causes the star’s spectrum to oscillate, with spectral lines shifting from redder wavelengths as the star moves away from us to bluer ones as the star moves toward us. The shift is due to a phenomenon called the Doppler effect . “Something similar occurs with gravitational waves,” said Scott Noble, a theoretical astrophysicist at NASA Goddard and a coauthor on the confirmation paper. “By themselves, double white dwarfs will emit gravitational waves at a nearly continuous frequency. science.description: null A robot just played Tinkertoys in space, assembling the first satellite structure ever made without a human touching the controls. The DARPA-funded project saw a robotic "truss builder" create a reflective antenna using Kapton film, composite fiber tubes and aluminum joints. The implications are huge for future missions, potentially opening up new possibilities to build — or fix — satellites in the final frontier. "This is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space ," Sergio Pellegrino, an aerospace and civil engineering professor at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement on Nov. 5 . The need for such spacecraft will likely rise substantially in the future, as companies assemble giant megaconstellations for cell-phone communications, AI compute and other purposes. Indeed, the ball is already rolling on such ambitious projects, generating enough hype for space startups around the globe to raise a record $20.8 billion in the third quarter of 2026 alone. Anything that launches aboard a rocket is limited by the size of that vehicle's fairing — the nose cone that protects payloads during their ride to space. In space, however, the ability to stretch out is practically infinite — after taking into account, of course, engineering and financing constraints. Assembling structures robotically off Earth could therefore be revolutionary, advocates say. And the recent milestone was a step in that direction. "This work could be useful not only for astronomy and astrophysics, but also for communications and other areas, such as building very large solar arrays for space solar power ," said Pellegrino, who's team leader of the truss-building project, a Caltech demonstration mission called Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA). ASTRA built a 1.4-meter-wide (4.5-foot) structure in orbit. That's an impressive achievement, but it just scratches the surface of what DARPA wants to accomplish via a program it calls Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design, or NOM4D for short. "NOM4D's objective is to enable efficient, scalable construction of very large structures in space," NOM4D Program Manager Andrew Detor said in a Nov. 5 DARPA statement . science.title: Curiosity Mars rover sizes up new 'Nazca' dig site | Space photo of the day for Nov. 10, 2026
science.description: null NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this close-up image using its Mars Hand Lens Imager, showing the abundance of disc-shaped potential crystal forms on our next drill target, dubbed "Nazca." (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it. What is it? Curiosity snapped the close-up image on Oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target. MAHLI is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image. Why is it incredible? Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow. The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

This 35 by 35 target is based on analysis by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) on what is needed to keep the 1.5°C global warming target within reach. Currently, electricity is estimated to make up just 23.4 per cent of the energy delivered to consumers, known as final energy – a figure that has increased by only 6.7 percentage points since 2000. This means that hitting the target will require the rate of electrification to quadruple compared with the first quarter of the 21st century and triple compared with the rate between 2020 and 2025. Judit Hecke at New Climate Institute, a German think tank, says such an acceleration is possible but “the challenge is getting policies, investment and infrastructure moving at the same pace”. Advertisement Progress on renewable energy has been encouraging, with renewables making up a higher proportion of overall electricity production year after year, and renewable capacity additions have been setting new records each year. In 2024, the most recent IRENA data, nearly 32 per cent of global electricity production came from renewable sources compared with just 18 per cent in 2000. Renewable energy capacity has increased from 0.8 terawatts in 2000 to 5.2 terawatts in 2025. But this is a long way from the COP28 pledge for UN member states to reach 11 terawatts of renewable capacity by 2030. However, Hecke points out that the electrification target includes electricity regardless of how it is generated, meaning that a country could make progress while still heavily relying on coal and gas in the power sector. Not only has Emily been proved right, but perhaps she didn’t go quite far enough. With remarkable prescience, Robinson even tipped Harrison’s Signs of Life as one of those books. As Harrison himself told the BBC’s Front Row last month, he has “been working for 40 to 50 years to shift the balance, both as a novelist and as a critic… Why shouldn’t a well written SF be considered to be literary fiction?”. His win is being trumpeted today as the first time a science fiction novel has won the Booker prize. science.title: Total solar eclipse 2027 vs 2028 — Which one should you choose, Egypt or Australia?
science.description: null For those who want to experience a total solar eclipse, the next two years present the best kind of problem. On Aug. 2, 2027, the so-called "eclipse of the century " will sweep across southern Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, bringing more than six minutes of totality to parts of Egypt. Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island. Both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences. The 2027 event combines over six minutes of totality with some of the very best weather prospects possible, while 2028 offers over five minutes of totality above some of the world's most famous wildernesses and cityscapes. Eclipse chasing requires careful planning and dedication, but also significant funds. If you can only choose one, which should it be? 2027 total solar eclipse: pros and cons A map of the 2027 total solar eclipse path. (Image credit: Michael Zeiler/EclipseAtlas.com) On paper, 2027 is difficult to beat. Maximum totality on Aug. 2 will last about 6 minutes, 23 seconds, making it the longest totality on land since 1991 and until 2114. The path of totality will cross southern Spain and Gibraltar before sweeping across Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Somalia and the Chagos Islands. About 88.9 million people live in its path, according to Time and Date . It will dominate the news for weeks. For Europeans, southern Spain is the obvious easy option. Tarifa, at the country's southern tip, will see about 4 minutes, 39 seconds of totality, while the U.K. Overseas Territory of Gibraltar gets about 4 minutes, 25 seconds. Travel farther east and the duration increases, with Sfax in Tunisia getting around 5 minutes, 41 seconds and locations in Egypt experiencing more than six minutes. Weather prospects generally improve, too, as the path crosses the deserts of North Africa. Egypt is the headline destination. Luxor will see about 6 minutes, 20 seconds of totality near midday, with Karnak Temple, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the world's greatest ancient monuments nearby. The climatic odds are excellent, with clouds extremely rare in early August. That combination of a very long totality, ancient landscapes and a very high probability of a clear sky makes 2027's path of totality highly unusual. But there are downsides. science.title: NASA's twin ESCAPADE Mars probes slingshot around Earth in unprecedented double 'gravity assist'
science.description: null Twin NASA spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long escapade, ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet. The Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE) spacecraft launched in November 2025 on the second-ever flight of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory . Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars . "No NASA mission has ever done this before," said Rob Lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and principal investigator of the ESCAPADE mission. "For most missions, it just isn't necessary." That's because traditionally NASA's Mars missions have been carefully choreographed within cosmic launch constraints, leaving Earth during a brief window of planetary alignment that only occurs every 26 months. ESCAPADE was meant to launch in October 2024, when Earth and Mars were favorably aligned, but delays with the New Glenn rocket forced the mission to sit out the precious launch window. Rather than wait to launch this fall, NASA decided to try something new. ESCAPADE mission planners designed a "loitering" orbit , shaped like a kidney bean. It called for the twin probes to loop through that trajectory to be back at Earth in early November 2026, ready to continue on to Mars. The ESCAPADE mission's unique path to reach Mars. After launching in November 2025, the twin ESCAPADE probes looped around the Earth-Sun Lagrange point 2 (L2), in a "loiter" orbit that returned them to Earth in November 2026 where they used our planet's gravity to slingshot themselves to Mars. (Image credit: Advanced Space/Matt Bolliger) Once they arrived, however, the twin probes faced a major hurdle: Each had to perfectly execute an engine burn within Earth's gravity well. The maneuver is similar to the slingshot flybys that spacecraft regularly conduct to adjust their trajectories — but here, the probes had to fire their engines to amp up the effect of the burn rather than acting alone. The first spacecraft tackled the feat on Nov. 7; the second did so on Monday (Nov. 9). And according to NASA, the burns went perfectly. "This is the first time NASA has used a powered Earth flyby to propel a spacecraft toward Mars, and we've now executed this maneuver twice, flawlessly, in just two days," Asal Naseri, acting associate flight director for NASA's Heliophysics Division said in a statement .
